title: Immutability and copying
learningObjectives: Explain immutability and copying and reason about JavaScript execution and function behaviour.

understand.concept: Immutability means treating existing data as unchanged and creating updated copies instead. Object spread and array methods such as map and filter create shallow copies. Structured cloning can copy supported structured data more deeply, but functions and some special values are not cloneable.
understand.whyItMatters: Immutable updates make state changes easier to track and reduce accidental side effects. Shallow copies still share nested references, so nested updates need deliberate copying.
understand.analogy: Instead of editing the original worksheet, make a revised copy and keep the earlier version intact.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scope, execution, identity, and scheduling follow language and engine semantics.

explain.narrative: The original scores array is unchanged. The updated object and its scores array are new references.
